title: Make study selectable; Athena resolves and pins firstmate's SHA at start
summary: Add the missing [capabilities.study] section so study is selectable. Add a core hook so that Athena's own networked code resolves firstmate's ref to a full SHA and records it when a study starts. The producer has no network and only reads the pinned, read-only source.

defaults_applied.how: The resolver and hook are Rust; the only non-Rust edits are the required TOML and Markdown.
Offline unit tests for the resolver and hook, with clippy and tests passing.
The SHA is resolved by code and the producer grant has no network commands, rather than by prompt instruction.
Reuse the existing athena-git helpers and the git binary before adding any crate.
CHANGELOG and decision notes cite the earlier rejected attempt's findings.
One change covers the selectable section and SHA pinning; the run step and the rest stay out.

assumptions: Reading: study is registered in crates/athena-cli/src/wiring.rs but absent from athena.toml, so it is not selectable. I read this from the repository; the study unit test also asserts the section is absent.
Athena's own process has network access and runs git for resolution. Agents have none, as the request says.
The resolved tree is checked out or exported read-only into the job directory, and the SHA is written to records and passed through the study env, e.g. ATHENA_STUDY_SOURCE_SHA.
The firstmate repository URL is not in the repository files I read, so the producer must take it from the user's answer or a clearly marked config key.
Only the SHA-resolution and checkout path is in scope; the full run step, replay and publishing stay deferred (D65).
question: What is firstmate's repository URL (and the ref to resolve, e.g. main)? I found neither in the repository files I could read.

acceptance_criteria.text: athena.toml gains [capabilities.study] with producer_commands (no rm/mv/chmod wildcard, no network-capable commands such as git fetch, clone or curl), verifier_commands (read-only), checks, and env; it also names firstmate's repository URL and the ref to resolve, and holds no hand-typed SHA. athena.toml is named in this criterion as a governance-file change.

A Capability hook with a default no-op body (so `change` is unchanged) lets the core call a capability when a job starts. Study implements it in Athena's Rust code, not in a prompt or producer command: it resolves the configured ref to a full 40-hex SHA, makes the tree available read-only, and records the SHA in the job's records and the producer's environment or brief.
The core invokes this hook in the job-start path, so a study job actually resolves and records the SHA. Nothing is left uncalled.
The producer prompt says the source is pinned, read-only and present, and that claims must cite the recorded full SHA. It has no other rewording.
CHANGELOG.md and docs/decisions.md state that Athena resolves firstmate's SHA at study start, that the producer has no network, and that no SHA is hand-recorded. They do not say a user must add one.

The reader's catalog lists `study` because its section is now in athena.toml. The wiring test for registered capabilities still passes. The study test that asserted the capability is absent from athena.toml is updated.

Run `cargo test --locked`. Offline tests, using an injected runner or a local fixture repository, cover: resolving a ref to a full SHA; rejecting a short, non-hex or empty result; rejecting an unresolvable ref; the hook being a no-op for `change`; and the hook being called at study start.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check`; both pass.

out_of_scope: Letting the producer fetch, clone or choose the SHA
The study run step, replay, containment and publishing (D65)
Rewording the producer prompt beyond the pinned read-only source and SHA citation
departures: Higher cost and time than the reference: the change spans core, capability and config, and the earlier attempt failed verification.
